summary: Pair 2 clears the bar across all six categories. ALIGNMENT (4): D2.1 expectation text is byte-identical to input_row.json; the expanded_walkthrough explicitly bridges to/from neighbouring days ('Yesterday Lucky reviewed likelihood. Today Mae introduces complementary events... Lesson 3 spinners; Lesson 4 dice; Lesson 5 capstone.'). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH (4): trap is named as the outcome-orientation phenomenon citing Konold (1989) AND Jones, Langrall, Thornton & Mogill (1997) Level-2 transition; recovery_moves branch by diagnostic (A: child names event but not complement; B: partial complement; C: complement not seen as probability event), each with concrete teacher action. INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE (4): puppets are OPTIONAL with explicit no-puppet substitutes (two distinct voices / stuffed animals / paper-bag / pictures on poster); movement-learners differentiation gives a body-based no-paper path ('one stands, one sits'); 12/25/13 = 50 min fits Grade 2. CLARITY_VOICE (4): Mae has a distinctive quotable refrain — 'EVENT — and its OPPOSITE!' / 'Both are POSSIBLE!' — opened in minds_on and chanted 3x in exit_routine; all success_criteria start with 'I can'. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY (4): action step 6 is an explicit STRATEGY COMPARE — child-generated pairs are brought to the carpet, class votes and justifies, citing Konold (1989) outcome-orientation ('true complements partition all outcomes; partial complements miss the gap'); Mae's gloss 'A real complement leaves NO GAPS. Together they cover everything that could happen.' is precise probability language at Grade 2. LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY (4): Parts 1/2/3 mirror Stations A/B/C, but Part 2 introduces unfamiliar pairs (Big/Small, Happy/Sad) not drilled in the minds_on list — a transfer task verifying generalization; early-finisher prompt extends the lesson's non-strict-complement discussion.
